proofs.title: Decidability Boundary Proof
proofs.explanation: Demonstrating structural undecidability constraints using self-reference loops.
steps: Suppose a structural decider machine H handles all input programs.
Construct a malicious evaluator program D that runs H on itself.
Design D to do the structural opposite of what H predicts.
Observe a direct logical contradiction, completing the reduction.

quiz.q: What core parameters distinguish optimisation problems from decision algorithms?
options: Decision models output a single binary verification bit; optimisation structures target an absolute maximum/minimum bounds metric.
Optimisation tasks use non-deterministic configurations exclusively.
There are no functional differences between them.
quiz.feedback: Decision bounds limit output criteria to YES/NO, whereas operational optimisation strategies balance objective evaluation metrics.
